title: GET /api/box/operator-config (200) and PATCH /api/box/operator-config (200)
description: The authoritative operator runtime configuration. Source: src/box/routes.ts, composed from the immutable snapshot in src/box/operatorConfig/snapshot.ts. A successful PATCH returns this SAME shape, so a client always ends a mutation holding the new authoritative state rather than having to re-read. `version` is the optimistic-concurrency token for the configuration AS A WHOLE: a PATCH echoes the version it believes it is editing and is refused if anything has moved, and the frontend also uses it to DISCARD a stale response that arrives after a newer one. `deployment` is READ-ONLY and env-owned — the four live-capability gates are displayed so an operator can see the deployment's ceiling, and no runtime write can alter them, which is what makes it impossible to turn a paper deployment live from a browser. `state` carries the facts the mutation policies are evaluated against, so the UI can explain a refusal before the operator attempts one. NO SECRET APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THIS PAYLOAD. CLOSED at every level so an added field is caught.

version.description: Monotonic configuration version. Increments by exactly one per accepted mutation.

operator_role.description: The requesting operator's role, as the BACKEND resolved it from the session cookie. The UI must not infer permission any other way.

deployment.description: Env/deployment-owned capability. READ-ONLY: no field here is writable through any runtime API. Runtime controls may only REMOVE permission beneath this ceiling, never widen it.

execution_mode.description: Which execution engine was CONSTRUCTED at startup. Immutable for the life of the process.

live_capable.description: Whether this deployment can place a real order AT ALL, as the backend computes it from the gates above and the active broker. The single authoritative paper/live signal for the UI — never derived client-side, and never from a stream's connection state.

state.description: The facts mutation policies are evaluated against. Backend-computed, so the UI can show why a change is currently refused without guessing.

flat.description: All five conditions together: no open box, no residual leg, no working order, nothing in flight, reconciliation clean. Computed by the backend so the UI cannot disagree about what flat means.

settings.description: Every registered setting. Non-empty: an empty list would read as 'nothing is configurable', which would hide the entire risk surface.

recent_changes.description: A short, newest-first slice of the append-only audit trail.
